subject: EvaluatorHost expression goldens (13 TEST_CASEs, 26 SECTIONs): '2+3'=5, '17 % 5'=2, '(2+3)*4-1'=19; "hello" + " " + "world"; [10,20,30] select 1=20; count [1,2,3,4]=4; logic and comparisons; Execute('x = 42'); if (true) then {1} =1; if (false) then {1} else {2} =2; while {wc < 5} do {wc = wc + 1} -> 5; {s = s + _x} forEach [1,2,3] -> 6; call {1} =1; format ["%1", HDSIN] with HDSIN undefined -> 'scalar bool array string 0xfcffffef'; private-array call using while "_i < 3" do {...} -> [0,1,2]; nulars time, isServer, pi.
rationale: The most valuable golden set in the evaluator suites: string +, select, count, if/then/else (else binds tighter than then because else is functionFirst), while/do, forEach/_x, call returning the last value, the private array form, the legacy string-condition form while "cond" do {..}, and the undefined-value sentinel the campaign bootstrap needs because 1.99 has no isNil (docs/research/18). The mock EvalFormat (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:91-129) uses the same algorithm as engine StrFormat (engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExtWorld.cpp:696-737), so the sentinel golden carries over. Drop time=0 and isServer=true (mock stubs). The private-scoping case '{...} call []' is mistyped (binary call needs code on the right, engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1149) and passes trivially: re-author as '[] call {...}' and mark adapted.

subject: format command (5 TEST_CASEs): format ["%1 + %2 = %3", 1, 2, 3] -> '1 + 2 = 3'; format ["%1=%2", "x", "y"] -> 'x=y' (strings unquoted); format ["hello world"] unchanged; format ["%1 is %2", "answer", 42] -> 'answer is 42'; hint format [...] -> host output '[HINT] 1=2'.
rationale: Needed for the format-placeholder lint (%N vs argument count) and for the reference evaluator's value rendering used by the campaign nil-check idiom. The mock EvalFormat (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:91-129) mirrors engine StrFormat (engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExtWorld.cpp:696-737): strings inserted unquoted, other values via GetText; %0 or an out-of-range %N is dropped silently (worth a lint warning). Scalars render as %g (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1980), 6 significant digits: 1234567 -> '1.23457e+06'. Adapt the last case by asserting the format result, not the mock '[HINT] ' prefix.

subject: EvaluatorHost API (3 TEST_CASEs): EvaluateExpression('hint "hello"') -> exit 0 and '[HINT] hello'; EvaluateSqfFile(utility_functions.sqf); EvaluateSqsFile(mission_init.sqs).
rationale: Embedding API of CWR's standalone evaluator (real parser plus mock world). A pattern for a possible script-lang check/run CLI or AI-agent dry run; nothing to port until such a tool exists.

subject: Synthetic mission scripts run through SqsRunner/EvaluateMultiple on the mock world (7 TEST_CASEs): patrol.sqs (3 waypoints), damage_monitor.sqs, mission_init.sqs (West group 3 units, leader SyntheticOfficerWest, ...), squad_management.sqf, utility_functions.sqf (Sum 15, Max 9), SQF exec of patrol.sqs, [west, 5] call _makeSquad.
fixture_notes: tests/fixtures/evaluator/{patrol,damage_monitor,mission_init}.sqs and {squad_management,utility_functions}.sqf (CWR-authored synthetic scripts, GPL-3.0-or-later with section 7 terms).
rationale: Execution needs a mock world (createGroup, createUnit, units, leader, setDammage, getVariable) outside the first milestones. Parsing is command-table-driven (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1797-1831): mission_init.sqs, squad_management.sqf and utility_functions.sqf use mock-only unary 'createUnit [..]'/'createVehicle [..]' and setVariable/getVariable (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:494-495, 691-692), whereas the engine has binary createUnit/createVehicle (engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExt.cpp:1335-1336) and no set/getVariable. Under an engine-faithful table they must fail to parse (negative dialect tests). patrol.sqs and damage_monitor.sqs go into the positive corpus now.

subject: Mock world of the CWR evaluator CLI (29 TEST_CASEs, 28 SECTIONs): object/group registries; alive, typeOf, name, getPos/setPos, damage, setDir, isNull objNull, player; createGroup/createUnit/units/leader/join; side text WEST/EAST/GUER/CIV; distance 3-4-5 = 5; setVariable/getVariable; addAction ids 0, 1.
rationale: Tests CWR's CLI mock, not the engine. Keep side rendering WEST/EAST/GUER/CIV. Mock shapes that must not enter our command table: unary array-form createUnit/createVehicle and unary isNull on any value (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:347,494-495; the engine has binary createUnit/createVehicle and object/group isNull, engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExt.cpp:933-934,1335-1336) and set/getVariable. getDamage/allowDamage are CWR one-M aliases (GameStateExt.cpp:946,1244-1245); setDamage (1242) has no alias comment, so its 1.99 status needs a probe.

subject: Table-driven host parity (2 TEST_CASEs, 9 fixture runs): hello.sqf, clean.sqf ('10 + 20 = 30'), distance.sqf, variables.sqf, this_test.sqf with args, error.sqf ('x = 1 +' -> exit 1, stderr 'Error:'), mission_init.sqs, delay.sqs, this_sqs.sqs.
rationale: Parse-level expectations port now against an explicit dialect table: hello, clean, this_test, delay and this_sqs parse; error.sqf fails at the dangling + with EvalNum; distance, variables and mission_init fail under engine tables (mock-only unary createVehicle/createUnit, set/getVariable). Stdout parity needs the reference interpreter plus host stubs.

subject: call, exit and exec (5 TEST_CASEs): 42 call {_this + 1} =43; [10, 20] call {(_this select 0) + (_this select 1)} =30; EvaluateMultiple('exitWith 42') =42; Execute('exit') -> EvalOK; [] exec loop.sqs -> EvalOK.
fixture_notes: The exec case uses tests/fixtures/evaluator/loop.sqs (synthetic); the others need no files.
rationale: Binary call with _this is core (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1149): port 43 and 30. exit is an engine nular (engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExt.cpp:882): port as a command-table golden. Unary 'exitWith 42' is mock-only (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:763); the engine has only binary 'if (..) exitWith {..}' (express.cpp:1139), probably post-1.99, so that one case is not-applicable. The exec case becomes a parse/type check of '[] exec "file"' (engine exec is Void x String, GameStateExt.cpp:1322).

subject: SQS parsing and execution (16 TEST_CASEs). Parse goldens: comment and blank lines produce no lines; '#start'/'#end' labels at line indices 0 and 1 (names trimmed); '? _x > 5 : hint "big"' -> condition '_x > 5 ' (right side untrimmed) and statement; '@alive player' -> waitUntil; '~5' -> '__waituntil = _time+(5)' then suspendUntil; '&10' -> absolute suspendUntil. Execution: hint then exit, goto, conditional lines and goto, _this, delays skipped in non-realtime, label loop to 3, the HDSIN lazy-init idiom -> '[HINT] 0'.
rationale: SqsRunner::parseLine mirrors engine Script::ProcessLine (engine/Poseidon/Game/Scripting/Scripts.cpp:228-334), including the split at the first ':' that forbids ':' inside '?' conditions. The 7 parse-level cases are SQS grammar goldens (port now); execution cases port with the reference interpreter. Engine differences to encode: a 4096-byte line buffer (Scripts.cpp:169); no trimming of '@'/'&' text; the '~' expression is spliced into a 256-byte buffer (Scripts.cpp:266-267); goto is an ordinary unary command (engine/Poseidon/Game/Commands/GameStateExt.cpp:1058), not a textual match; a '?' line without ':' is silently dropped (Scripts.cpp:299-304; lint error). The '_this' case uses mock-only str (engine/Evaluator/EvalState.cpp:198): re-author with format ["%1", _this] and mark adapted. The HDSIN case is the 1.99 lazy-init idiom to reuse in the campaign bootstrap.

subject: Documentation-example validation (4 TEST_CASEs): validateBook extracts sqf code fences from a markdown chapter (pass, fail on undefined_func, skip); validateRef runs JSON command-reference examples (hint.json, addEventHandler.json); missing directory gives zero counts.
rationale: A doc-test idea for our command database: every example must parse and type-check. The JSON schema (name, arity, group, description, syntax, return_type, arg_types, examples) is a reasonable model for our static command table; only the two sample files exist upstream.

subject: Precedence, parentheses, variables, arrays and strings (26 TEST_CASEs, 41 SECTIONs): 2 + 3 * 4=14, 10 - 2 * 3=4, 2 * 3 ^ 2=18, 10 / 2 ^ 2=2.5, -(2 + 3)=-5, -2 * 3=-6, 2 * (3 + (4 * 5))=46. Globals set with VarSet: x + 5=15, a * b + 2=17, (x + y) * z=900, maxHealth - (damage * (1 - armor))=87.5. Array literals [1, 2, 3], [], [[1, 2], [3, 4]]. String == true/false. Twelve sections have no upstream oracle.
fixture_notes: Inline strings plus a few global scalar bindings.
rationale: Pins the priority table (engine/Evaluator/express.hpp:503-516), loosest to tightest: || or < && and < comparison < binary commands < else < + - < * / % mod atan2 < unary < ^ < parentheses. The DSL lowering uses it to place parentheses. Extra derived golden: '-2 ^ 2' = -4. Source-derived goldens for the no-oracle inputs (tag unverified-1.99): '(2 + 3' -> EvalCloseB and '2 + 3)' -> EvalOpenB (express.cpp:1739-1780); undefinedVar + 5 -> typed nil Scalar, EvalOK (express.cpp:1348-1351, 2432-2439); "Hello" + " World" -> "Hello World" (express.cpp:1119); '10 / 0' -> EvalDivZero; '3.14.159', '5 5', 'invalid syntax here' -> EvalOper (express.cpp:1822-1831); '5 + * 3', '5 +' -> EvalNum; Execute('_x = 5; _y = 10') on the global state -> EvalNamespace (express.cpp:2557-2562); EvaluateMultiple('10; 20; 30') -> 30 (express.cpp:2702-2771).

subject: GameData concrete classes (38 TEST_CASEs, 67 SECTIONs): Scalar/Bool/String/Array/Nil/Nothing construction, GetType, GetScalar, GetText (Nothing -> 'nothing'), GetTypeName (Scalar 'float', Nil 'void'), IsEqualTo, Clone, read-only flag, mixed and nested arrays.
rationale: Object-model internals, not ported one-to-one. Rendering facts for our value-to-text function (format, str, nil-check idiom): scalars %g (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1977-1982), bools true/false (2000-2003), arrays [a,b] (2056+), untyped nil 'scalar bool array string 0xfcffffef' (1908-1913). A typed nil renders as its type list such as 'scalar' (1918-1937), so the sentinel idiom only detects an untyped nil read directly from an undefined variable.

subject: Robustness and boundaries (14 TEST_CASEs, 28 SECTIONs): fuzz regressions (CheckExecute on 4-byte heap buffers 'x=1' and 'pri'; a 300-char identifier); 100 chained additions = 101; 500-char string literal; 20 nested parens around 5 = 5; whitespace variants ('   5   +   3   '=8, tab/newline separated 10 + 20 = 30, '2+2'=4); repeated evaluation and 100-variable stress; escape and extreme-number inputs (no oracle); 'tcrash_arr resize -10000' -> empty array; refcount/leak sections.
fixture_notes: Inline or generated strings. The '54 fuzzer reproducers' mentioned in comments are in neither repo (apps/fuzzers ships no corpus).
rationale: Robustness goldens for the Rust lexer/parser (no panic on any input); seed a cargo-fuzz corpus with them. Refcount/leak sections do not apply. SQF has no backslash escapes, quotes are doubled (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:222-256): the backslash-quote input must give EvalOper, and 'line1\nline2' is a literal backslash-n. Numbers are f32 (express.hpp:444): 999999999999 evaluates to about 1e12 and renders '1e+12' via %g. The real limit is the 256-slot operand stack per statement (SL, express.hpp:446; EvalLineLong at express.cpp:1641-1645), not paren depth: array literals of 256+ elements fail, so the campaign compiler must split large generated arrays. Negative resize corrupted the heap in unfixed code: lint it as an error-level hazard and probe expecting a possible crash (resize may be post-1.99, docs/research/19 F5).

subject: Unary-function registration API (13 TEST_CASEs, 18 SECTIONs): NewFunction, AppendFunctionList with prefix filters, overloads by argument type, return types, 'nonexistentfunc 5' must not crash.
rationale: A runtime-extensible registry we will not have. Design facts for the static command table: names are case-insensitive keys (engine/Evaluator/express.hpp:497), one name maps to an overload set chosen by operand type, prefix enumeration supports autocompletion. The only portable behavior is 'unknown unary command -> diagnostic'.

subject: C++-driven scenario workflows (10 TEST_CASEs, 10 SECTIONs) that VarSet globals and Evaluate arithmetic between C++ branches: health bookkeeping (75 then 60), counter + 1 to 10, velocity * 0.707, (vy * 2) / gravity, (20 * 20) + (10 * 10), ammo and magazine bookkeeping, (velocity / 2) * totalTime=2.5.
rationale: Only the SQF strings matter; the C++ loops become Rust test code. Same machinery as test_evaluator_complex, so port together; marginal value is low.

subject: Nular registration API (12 TEST_CASEs, 19 SECTIONs): NewNularOp/AppendNularOpList, bulk registration; a nular and a global variable of the same name coexist and VarGet returns the variable (200); unknown nular must not crash.
rationale: The core evaluator defines only nil, true, false and pi as nulars (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1210-1212); player, time, west etc. come from the game layer and our table must list them. Resolution order from source: at run time a defined global shadows a nular/unary/binary command of the same name (express.cpp:195, 1320, 1394, 1624, 1806); in check mode the command wins. Assigning a global named like a command (count, alive) passes editor validation but changes later parses: make it a lint error and confirm with a 1.99 probe.

subject: Runtime registration of custom binary operators and priorities (11 TEST_CASEs, 15 SECTIONs): '5 @@ 3'=18, '2 ## 3 * 4'=14, '10 $$ 5'=15, same-priority left-to-right '2 << 3 >> 4'=20; unknown operator and type mismatch (no oracle); AppendOperatorList.
rationale: Our command table is static data, so runtime registration does not apply. Portable semantics: same-priority operators associate left and priority slots decide binding. Port verbatim only if the parser is table-driven and tests may inject a table; otherwise restate with built-ins (10 - 2 - 3 = 5, 2 * 3 / 4 = 1.5, 2 + 3 * 4 = 14). One case accepts {14,19}: no single oracle.

subject: Evaluator reentrancy regression (VyhodFrameGuard, 5 TEST_CASEs): identity unary functions call Evaluate() inside their handler; '5 + f 7 + 11'=23, '100 + g 50 + 200'=350, 'f 1 + f 2 + f 4 + f 8'=15, '1000 + h 500'=1500; GetLastError stays EvalOK.
rationale: A Rust parser without global mutable state cannot have this bug. The expressions are not parse-shape goldens: the handlers are identities, so '(f 7) + 11' and 'f (7 + 11)' both give 23. Add our own golden with a non-linear unary to pin binding: 'sqrt 16 + 9' = 13, because unary outranks + (engine/Evaluator/express.hpp:503-516).

subject: Mission-style expressions over globals set with VarSet (10 TEST_CASEs, 11 SECTIONs): health - damage=70; chained damage to 55; (dx * dx) + (dy * dy)=125; unitAmmo - 3=27; force / mass=5; accel * deltaTime=0.5; objComplete / objTotal=1; health < threshold true then false after healing; health <= 0; (shotsHit / shotsFired) * 100=75; (enemiesKilled * 100) / (shotsFired / 10)=100.
fixture_notes: No files; scalar bindings supplied in the test.
rationale: Arithmetic and comparisons over global scalars are the shape of lowered campaign guard conditions and need only the global-scalar environment test_evaluator_complex already needs. Port as goldens and reuse as equivalence tests (DSL evaluation == SQF reference evaluation of the lowered text).

subject: GameState::Evaluate/EvaluateBool on literals and core operators (23 TEST_CASEs, 87 SECTIONs). Literals 42, 0, -123, 3.14, .5, "hello", "", true/false. Arithmetic goldens: 10 + 5=15, 10 + 2.5=12.5, 5 - (-3)=8, -5 * -3=15, 10 / 3~3.33333, 10 / -2=-5, 10 % 3=1, 100 % 7=2, 2 ^ 8=256, 16 ^ 0.5=4, (-2) ^ 2=4. Comparisons ==, !=, <, >, <=, >= on scalars (Bool result, equal-value edges); "test" == "test". Full &&, ||, ! truth tables; EvaluateBool('5 > 3'). Five sections have no upstream oracle: '10 / 0', '', '5 +', '5 @ 3', '(5 + 3'.
fixture_notes: Inline SQF strings only. Copy every literal expected value into a Rust golden table (f32 + epsilon).
rationale: Core expression semantics for the lexer, parser, type checker and constant folder, and the truth tables the campaign condition DSL lowers to. '-123' is unary minus applied to 123, not a negative literal (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1610-1647); '.5' parses because numbers go through strtod (express.cpp:139-150). There is no short-circuit: 'false && (10 / 0)' ends as EvalType because the only && overload is Bool x Bool (express.cpp:1123) and SetError overwrites the earlier EvalDivZero (express.cpp:93-95, 382-388). Port the five no-oracle sections as source-derived goldens tagged unverified-1.99: '10 / 0' -> EvalDivZero; '' -> Scalar 0 with EvalOK (express.cpp:2656-2659); '5 +' -> EvalNum; '5 @ 3' -> EvalOper; '(5 + 3' -> EvalCloseB.

subject: GameState variable API (19 TEST_CASEs, 33 SECTIONs): VarSet/VarGet/VarDelete/VarLocal, forceLocal, VarReadOnly; IdtfGoodName valid (validName, _underscore, name123, CamelCase) and invalid ('', 123start, 'has space', has-dash); VarGoodName/LValueGoodName; BeginContext/EndContext with nested spaces; GetVariables enumeration; globals survive local contexts.
rationale: IdtfGoodName defines the identifier rule [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:152-160, 2800-2814), needed by the lexer and by validation of variable, unit and marker names. VarGet/VarSet lowercase every name (express.cpp:2406-2411, 2551-2556): SQF variables are case-insensitive, so campaign variables must be unique ignoring case. Reading '_x' with no local scope raises EvalNamespace (express.cpp:2423-2429). About 16 assertions are tautological.

subject: Check-mode syntax validation without execution (12 TEST_CASEs, 32 SECTIONs). CheckEvaluate true: '2 + 2', '(10 + 20) * (30 - 5)', '[1, 2, 3]', a string literal, '2 + 3 * 4 - 5 / 2'; false: '(2 + 3', '5 + * 3', '5 +'. CheckEvaluateBool true: 'true && false', '5 > 3'; false: 'true &&'. CheckExecute false: '= 5'. GetLastErrorPos after errors; recovery '5 + 5'=10 after an error. About 19 sections have no upstream oracle (assignments, if/then/else, while/do, sqrt 16, select).
rationale: CheckEvaluateBool and CheckExecute are what the in-game editor calls to validate trigger/waypoint conditions, on-activation and init fields (engine/Poseidon/UI/Map/UIArcade.cpp:1106,1118,1719,1731,1743; UIArcadeWaypoint.cpp:331,343), so editor-core field validation must accept and reject the same text. 13 definite cases. Check mode is deterministic from source: unknown globals type as any (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:195-219), handlers never run and {...} bodies are opaque strings, so every no-oracle case checks valid; '' is valid (express.cpp:2656-2659); after success GetLastError is EvalOK (express.cpp:2643). Error text and caret position are user-visible (UIArcade.cpp:1106-1111; position set at express.cpp:110-111): port engine-compatible caret offsets as editor-ui goldens, do not invent spans.

subject: GameValue wrapper (26 TEST_CASEs, 72 SECTIONs): typed constructors, implicit casts (Bool->Scalar 1/0), SharedInstance vs Duplicate, read-only arrays, GetText quotes strings, type-strict IsEqualTo (42 vs "42" false, 0 vs false false).
rationale: C++ handle mechanics that a Rust enum replaces. Facts kept for the value model: equality is type-strict and 'in'/'find' use it (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:1085-1092); strings are quoted by GetText but not by format %N; arrays are shared by reference (array-aliasing caveat in docs/research/19).

subject: GameVarSpace scope chain (18 TEST_CASEs, 28 SECTIONs): set/get/overwrite, not-found, read-only flag, three-level parent lookup, VarSet on a child updates an existing parent binding, VarLocal isolation, raw-level case sensitivity, 100-variable store.
rationale: Reference for the linter's scope/dataflow model: assignment writes the nearest existing binding, only 'private' introduces a new one, and assigning nil destroys a variable only in the outermost scope (engine/Evaluator/express.cpp:2486-2530). Do not port the case-sensitivity test as a language rule: GameState lowercases names before they reach GameVarSpace.

subject: EntityEvent enum has exactly 12 names in legacy order: Killed, Hit, Engine, GetIn, GetOut, Fired, IncomingMissile, Dammaged, Gear, Fuel, AnimChanged, Init (name <-> value round trip).
rationale: The event-handler name table for addEventHandler validation and CfgVehicles EventHandlers linting. Port as a static table test; confirm on 1.99 that Init is config-only.

subject: Float helpers: saturate, fastRound, fastFloor; toInt rounds half to even like x86 fistp; toLargeInt; toIntFloor/Ceil; myLower/myUpper.
rationale: Engine float-to-int conversion rounds half to even (Czech lip-sync regression). Relevant wherever script-lang lowering or validation depends on engine numeric conversion.

subject: Script particle command drop: GetVector3 maps a script array [100,200,0] to engine Vector3 (100,0,200), so script positions are [x, north, height] while the engine uses (x, height, north); IsParticleDropArgumentCountSupported accepts 18 or 19 arguments, rejects 17 and 20; compile check.
rationale: Script-language facts hidden in a Graphics file: drop arity for the linter and the position axis swap.
